record.paper_title: The 1999 Heineman Prize Address Integrable models in statistical mechanics: The hidden field with unsolved problems
record.original_question: For integrable statistical-mechanical models away from criticality, can the correlation functions be characterized by nonlinear classically integrable equations—differential, integral, or difference equations—in a way that extends the Ising-model Painleve and difference-equation descriptions and generalizes the linear equations that describe correlation functions in conformal field theory at the critical point to the massive case?

evidence.quote: Conjecture The correlation functions of integrable statistical mechanical models are characterized as the solutions of classically integrable equations (be they dif�erential, integral or difference).

One of the major unsolved problems of integrable models today is to extend the linear equations which characterize correlation functions in conformal field theory to nonlinear equations for massive models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two-dimensional integrable statistical-mechanical lattice models (or their massive quantum field theory scaling limits) away from criticality. For such a model, let $G(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ denote an $n$-point correlation function of local operators. It is known classically that:

(i) For the two-dimensional Ising model, the diagonal two-point correlation functions can be expressed in terms of solutions of a Painlevé VI ordinary differential equation (and a Painlevé III equation in the scaling limit), and they satisfy nonlinear difference equations in the lattice variables.

(ii) For conformal field theories describing critical points, correlation functions satisfy linear differential equations (the Belavin–Polyakov–Zamolodchikov equations and their generalizations).

Problem. Prove or disprove the following conjecture: every correlation function of any integrable statistical-mechanical model (massive, i.e., off-critical) is characterized as a solution of a system of classically integrable nonlinear equations—of differential, integral, or difference type—in its arguments (positions, lattice spacings, coupling constants, or temperature). In other words, find a uniform mechanism that extends the Painlevé and nonlinear difference-equation description of Ising correlations to the correlation functions of all integrable massive models, and that reduces, at criticality, to the linear differential equations of conformal field theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a broad program-level question. Partial results exist: the Ising model (Painlevé III/VI, nonlinear difference equations), the impenetrable Bose gas and quantum nonlinear Schrödinger equation (classical integrable PDEs for correlators via determinant/Fredholm representations), and form-factor expansions for massive integrable QFTs. However, no general proof characterizing all correlation functions of every integrable massive model by classically integrable equations has been established, and the problem is still regarded as one of the major open problems in the field.

status_evidence.title: Completely Integrable Equation for the Quantum Correlation Function of Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Correlation functions of exactly solvable models can be described by differential equations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: correlation functions of the quantum NLS are described by a classical completely integrable equation, supporting the conjecture in this case.

status_evidence.title: Low temperature correlation functions in integrable models
status_evidence.snippet: Derivation of the large distance and time asymptotics from the form factor expansion.
status_evidence.claim: Form-factor methods give asymptotics but no universal nonlinear integrable equation for all massive integrable correlators.

status_evidence.title: Correlation Functions in 2-Dimensional Integrable Quantum Field Theories
status_evidence.snippet: Program to study correlation functions in massive integrable 2D relativistic field theories via form factors.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art for massive integrable QFT correlators is form-factor reconstruction, not a general nonlinear integrable-equation characterization.
